---
title: "The most common hospital infection is not the most harmful"
description: "Counting infections and measuring harm give different answers."
author: "Chenghuiyu Fan"
date: "2026-10-03"
categories: [health, data story]
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

burden <- tribble(
  ~infection, ~cases, ~dalys,
  "Pneumonia", 132.0, 86.1,
  "Urinary tract infection", 265.1, 82.6,
  "Bloodstream infection", 33.4, 72.2,
  "Surgical site infection", 115.4, 35.7,
  "C. difficile infection", 44.6, 25.9
)
```

The numbers in this post come from a study by @zacher2019.

```{r}
#| echo: false

burden_share <- burden |>
  mutate(
    cases_share = cases / sum(cases) * 100,
    dalys_share = dalys / sum(dalys) * 100,
    focus = if_else(infection == "Bloodstream infection", "Focus", "Context")
  )|>
  pivot_longer(c(cases_share, dalys_share), names_to = "measure", values_to = "share")|>
  mutate(
    measure = if_else(measure == "cases_share", "Share of all infections", "Share of healthy years lost")
  )
```

@fig-share shows two numbers for each infection.

```{r}
#| label: fig-share
#| fig-cap: "Bloodstream infection is 6% of all infections but causes 24% of the healthy years lost. Germany, 2011 and 2012."
#| fig-alt: "Two bar charts. Bloodstream infection has the shortest bar for share of infections and a long bar for share of healthy years lost."
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.8

focus_colours <- c("Context" = "#B8B8B8", "Focus" = "#0B4F6C")

ggplot(burden_share, aes(x = share, y = fct_reorder(infection, cases), fill = focus)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(share), "%")), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~measure) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = focus_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 55)) +
  labs(x = "Percentage of the total", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```
